name: Mvog-Betsi Zoo
description: A zoo and primate rescue center home to gorillas, chimpanzees and other native wildlife, run in partnership with conservation groups.

name: Monument de la Réunification
description: A landmark monument commemorating the reunification of French and British Cameroon, with a spiral viewing platform over the city.
image_attribution: Z. NGNOGUE, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Marche Central (Mfoundi Market)
description: Yaoundé's largest and busiest market, packed with textiles, produce, crafts and street food stalls.
image_attribution: Bdx, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Notre-Dame des Victoires Cathedral
description: A striking Catholic cathedral known for its architecture and as a quiet spot in the busy city center.

name: Mont Fébé
description: A hill overlooking the city with hiking trails, a hotel, and panoramic viewpoints popular at sunset.

name: Bastos Neighborhood
description: An upscale district known for restaurants, embassies, cafes and nightlife, popular with visitors and expats.

name: National Museum of Yaoundé
description: Housed in a former presidential palace, showcasing Cameroonian art, artifacts and royal regalia.

name: Nsimeyong
description: A lively residential neighborhood known for local food spots and everyday Yaoundé street life.

name: Mvog-Ada
description: A busy residential and commercial neighborhood, good for experiencing everyday Yaoundé away from the main tourist spots.

name: Etoa-Meki Market
description: A neighborhood market popular with locals for produce, household goods and everyday shopping.

name: Chefferie Traditionnelle d'Ekounou
description: A traditional chieftaincy site reflecting local customary institutions and heritage in the Ekounou area.

name: Yaoundé Golf Club
description: A long-established golf course offering a quiet, green recreational space in the middle of the city.

name: Stade Ahmadou Ahidjo
description: Yaoundé's main football stadium, hosting national matches and major sporting events.

name: Quartier du Gouvernement
description: The administrative district housing government ministries, known for its formal architecture and wide boulevards.

name: Hilton Yaoundé Viewpoint
description: A hilltop hotel known locally for one of the best panoramic views over central Yaoundé.

name: Université de Yaoundé I
description: The country's oldest public university, with a large green campus and a lively student atmosphere nearby.

name: Complexe Sportif de Yaoundé
description: A multipurpose sports complex used for athletics, basketball and community sporting events.

name: Essos Market
description: A neighborhood market known for fresh produce and a genuine, non-touristy shopping experience.

name: Nsam Market
description: A busy local market serving the Nsam neighborhood with produce, textiles and household goods.

name: Biyem-Assi Neighborhood
description: A large, lively residential neighborhood with a mix of local shops, food stalls and everyday city life.

name: Ngousso Neighborhood
description: A growing residential area on the edge of the city, offering a quieter, more local pace of life.

name: Mfoundi River Banks
description: A stretch of the river that runs through the city, offering a different, quieter view of Yaoundé's landscape.
